params.script_inline:
"""The surface: layout, markup, and the one write that keeps them honest. THIS FILE IS THE SOURCE. `config.json` carries a copy of it in `script_inline`, generated by `scripts/canvy_sync.py` and pinned by a test in `crates/meclaw-cells/tests/canvy_template.rs`. Edit here, then run: python3 scripts/canvy_sync.py Why the copy exists at all: a `code` cell's `script_path` is handed to the interpreter verbatim with no working directory of its own (the factory ignores `cell_dir` — `code` is stateless), so a relative path would resolve against the daemon's cwd, and an absolute path baked into a template is the exported-tree defect class of GH #20. So the runtime form is `script_inline`, and this file is what a person reads, greps, diffs and runs: python3 templates/canvy/render/render.py < some-store-answer.json # What this cell is, and what it is not It is the whole picture. Every tag, every colour, every coordinate is decided here, which is what makes a new object type a template change instead of a release. The binary that serves it knows none of this. It is NOT the owner of the topology. That comes from `/colony/graph`, by message, into this hive's own store, on a timer — never read out of a database, and never fetched inside a browser's request (a `/colony` reply arrives on a fresh envelope with no context, so it could not be correlated back to the browser that asked). # The two passes Pass 1 (a request from the HTTP layer): remember what was asked in `hop`, emit one `select` over the whole `canvas` table. Pass 2 (the store's answer): compute the layout, render everything, emit the HTML on the surface lane — and, if the request carried a move, emit the layout write in the same pass. The box is rendered exactly where it is written, from one input, so the picture and the database cannot disagree. """ import json import sys import uuid # The layout constants, from the Python reference this ports (topology_html.py). NODE_W, NODE_H = 150, 38 GAP_X, GAP_Y = 60, 40 PAD_TOP, PAD_SIDE, PAD_BOT = 30, 24, 24 # How wide a shelf of hives may grow before the next one wraps to a new row, and # the air between two hive boxes. `SHELF_W` is a target and not a limit: a single # hive wider than this still gets its own row rather than being cut. SHELF_W = 2400 HIVE_GAP_X, HIVE_GAP_Y = 90, 80 # Fill and stroke per cell type. Ported verbatim from colony_topology.py so the # shipped surface and the standalone renderer draw the same colony. TYPE_COLOR = { "llm": ("#d6e4ff", "#4a6fa5"), "code": ("#e8e8e8", "#8a8a8a"), "file": ("#e8e8e8", "#8a8a8a"), "edit": ("#e8e8e8", "#8a8a8a"), "store": ("#ffe6cc", "#d79b00"), "proxy": ("#d5e8d4", "#82b366"), "timer": ("#fff2cc", "#d6b656"), "web_fetch": ("#f8cecc", "#b85450"), "web_search": ("#f8cecc", "#b85450"), "bash": ("#e1d5e7", "#9673a6"), "harness": ("#e1d5e7", "#9673a6"), "mcp": ("#e1d5e7", "#9673a6"), "vault": ("#f5f5f5", "#666666"), "subcolony": ("#dae8fc", "#6c8ebf"), } DEFAULT_COLOR = ("#ffffff", "#999999") def esc(s): """Escape for an HTML text node or a double-quoted attribute. Everything rendered here came out of a database, and a cell path with a `<` in it must not be able to close a tag. """ return ( str(s) .replace("&", "&") .replace("<", "<") .replace(">", ">") .replace('"', """) .replace("'", "'") ) def store_op(operation, **rest): """One store operation, on the lane the hive routes to its store. The four `moved_*`/`event` slots are set here, empty, on EVERY store emission and not only on the one that carries a drop. The hive's `./render -> ./store` edge promotes them into `context`, and an edge modifier that reads a hop field the emission does not have does not merely skip the promotion — the edge stops matching, so the emission dead-letters as `no_route`. That is how the position writes of a drop were silently lost while the picture still showed the box in its new place: the render reached the browser through a different edge, and only the two writes died. """ args = {"operation": operation} args.update(rest) return { "header": { "route": "canvas", "event": "", "moved_id": "", "moved_x": "", "moved_y": "", }, "messages": [ { "origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call", "id": uuid.uuid4().hex[:12], "text": json.dumps(args), } ], } def surface_reply(slot): """The answer the HTTP layer is waiting for, on the egress lane. The lane is `./render -> .`: the answer is handed to this hive, finds no out-edge there, and leaves through the colony's egress door. The door is not a place any more — a marked message (`EgressPolicy::Marked`, and only the HTTP layer can mint the mark) leaves from whichever hive it ran out of graph at, which is what makes this hive installable by mutation at all (GH #163). Before that fix the lane had to be `-> /`, and no mutation may draw an edge that leaves its own subtree. `messages: []` is mandatory and not decoration. Every body crossing the substrate is validated as a UBF document, and one without that slot is rejected as `invalid_ubf_body` — the emission never reaches an edge, so it shows up as a dead letter from this cell and as a join that times out with no other trace. The surface payload rides alongside in its own `surface` slot. """ return {"header": {"route": "surface"}, "messages": [], "surface": slot} def last_text(body): """The text of the last turn, or "" — the store puts its answer there.""" msgs = body.get("messages") or [] return str(msgs[-1].get("text") or "") if msgs else "" def rows_of(body): """The store's result, as rows, or None when it did not answer with rows. `None` here means "the store said something that is not a result set" — an error string, for instance. It must NOT be confused with "this is a fresh request": the passes are told apart by `context`, not by whether a body happens to parse. Getting that wrong once produced an infinite render/store loop that only stopped when the TTL ran out, and every store error would have produced it again. """ try: v = json.loads(last_text(body) or "null") except Exception: return None return v if isinstance(v, list) else None def fmt_scale(per_mille): """The camera's zoom as an SVG scale factor. Per-mille because a store column is `text`, `int` or `json` — there is no float, and a thousandth is finer than a mouse wheel can express. """ z = max(100, min(4000, int(per_mille or 1000))) return ("%.3f" % (z / 1000.0)).rstrip("0").rstrip(".") def as_doc(value): """A `json` column arrives as a string. Absent or unreadable → empty.""" if isinstance(value, dict): return value if isinstance(value, str) and value.strip(): try: v = json.loads(value) return v if isinstance(v, dict) else {} except Exception: return {} return {} # --- the tree the colony graph describes ------------------------------------- def hive_of(path): """The parent path of a cell, without its leading slash. "" at the root.""" p = path.strip("/") return p.rsplit("/", 1)[0] if "/" in p else "" def flow_layers(ids, edges): """A layer per node: one below every node that feeds it. Longest-path from the sources, with a visit cap so a cycle cannot spin. A colony graph has cycles by design (every request/reply pair is one), so this is a drawing heuristic and not a topological sort. """ incoming = {i: [] for i in ids} for e in edges: if e["from"] in incoming and e["to"] in incoming: incoming[e["to"]].append(e["from"]) layer = {i: 0 for i in ids} for _ in range(min(len(ids), 64)): changed = False for i in ids: want = max([layer[s] + 1 for s in incoming[i]], default=0) if want > layer[i]: layer[i] = want changed = True if not changed: break return layer def hive_block(members, layer): """One hive laid out on its own, relative to (0, 0): rows by flow rank. The flow layer is computed across the WHOLE graph, but it is applied inside one hive, so it has to be COMPRESSED here, not merely shifted. The global layer of a cell is the longest chain reaching it from anywhere, and a real colony has long chains: two cells in the same hive can carry layer 5 and layer 400 because one of them is downstream of a deep pipeline elsewhere. Shifting by the minimum leaves the 395 empty rows between them. Measured on a live 46-cell / 13-hive colony: y ran to 174828 with the raw layer, 52992 shifted, and 3384 ranked. What a hive's height should say is how many flow STEPS it has inside it, and ranking is what says that. The order is preserved, so a request still sits above the thing it asks. Returns `(relative positions, width, height)`. """ rank = {lv: r for r, lv in enumerate(sorted({layer[i] for i in members}))} rows = {} for i in members: rows.setdefault(rank[layer[i]], []).append(i) rel = {} width = 0 for lv in sorted(rows): x = 0 for i in rows[lv]: rel[i] = (x, lv * (NODE_H + GAP_Y)) x += NODE_W + GAP_X width = max(width, x - GAP_X) height = (max(rows) + 1) * (NODE_H + GAP_Y) - GAP_Y return rel, width, height def auto_layout(nodes, edges, saved): """Where every box sits. A saved position always wins. Two levels, and the outer one is the one that decides whether the picture is readable at all. Inside a hive: rows by flow rank (`hive_block`). Between hives: **packed into rows**, left to right, wrapping at `SHELF_W`. Stacking the hives in one column was the first version, and it was reported unusable on the first colony that had more than a handful: 14 hives became a 3672-pixel-tall strip two boxes wide. Every hive sat at the same x, so the whole arrangement carried exactly one bit of information — order — while a screen is two-dimensional. Packing is not decoration: it is what makes the default arrangement worth keeping long enough to rearrange it by hand. Sorted by hive path, so siblings land next to each other rather than wherever a dictionary happened to put them. Deterministic: same input, same output, so a changed picture means a changed colony. """ ids = [n["id"] for n in nodes] layer = flow_layers(ids, edges) by_hive = {} for n in nodes: by_hive.setdefault(hive_of(n["id"]), []).append(n["id"]) pos = {} shelf_x, shelf_y, shelf_h = PAD_SIDE, PAD_TOP, 0 for hive in sorted(by_hive): members = sorted(by_hive[hive], key=lambda i: (layer[i], i)) rel, w, h = hive_block(members, layer) # Wrap when this hive would push the row past the target width — but # never wrap an empty row, or a single hive wider than SHELF_W would # start on a line of its own forever. if shelf_x > PAD_SIDE and shelf_x + w > SHELF_W: shelf_y += shelf_h + HIVE_GAP_Y shelf_x, shelf_h = PAD_SIDE, 0 for i, (rx, ry) in rel.items(): pos[i] = (shelf_x + rx, shelf_y + ry) shelf_x += w + HIVE_GAP_X shelf_h = max(shelf_h, h) # A saved position always wins, and one saved box must not move its # neighbours: the automatic layout above is only the default for a box # nobody has touched. for i, xy in saved.items(): if i in pos: pos[i] = xy return pos def hive_boxes(nodes, pos): """One box per hive, derived from where its members ended up. Derived and never stored, which is what makes dragging a cell out of a crowd GROW its hive instead of stranding the cell outside a stale rectangle. """ groups = {} for n in nodes: h = hive_of(n["id"]) if not h: continue groups.setdefault(h, []).append(pos[n["id"]]) boxes = [] for h in sorted(groups): xs = [p[0] for p in groups[h]] ys = [p[1] for p in groups[h]] x = min(xs) - PAD_SIDE y = min(ys) - PAD_TOP w = (max(xs) + NODE_W + PAD_SIDE) - x ht = (max(ys) + NODE_H + PAD_BOT) - y boxes.append( { "id": h, "name": h.rsplit("/", 1)[-1], "depth": h.count("/") + 1, "x": x, "y": y, "w": w, "h": ht, } ) return boxes def edge_lanes(edges): """A lane number per edge, centred within its endpoint pair. Two passes, the same two the reference viewer did: number the edges inside each unordered pair, then shift the bundle so it straddles the centre line. Parallel edges between one pair then stay apart instead of overlapping. """ groups = {} for e in edges: key = tuple(sorted((e["from"], e["to"]))) groups.setdefault(key, []).append(e) for members in groups.values(): n = len(members) for k, e in enumerate(members): e["lane"] = k - (n - 1) // 2 return edges # --- markup ------------------------------------------------------------------- def node_svg(n): # `data-node` is what the drag hook grabs; `data-from`/`data-to` on an edge is # how it finds the lines belonging to a box without being told. return ( '' '' '%s' '%s' "" ) % ( esc(n["id"]), NODE_W, NODE_H, n["x"], n["y"], NODE_W, NODE_H, esc(n["fill"]), esc(n["stroke"]), esc(n["name"]), esc(n["type"]), ) def hive_svg(h): return ( '' '' '%s' "" ) % ( esc(h["id"]), h["x"], h["y"], h["w"], h["h"], h["x"] + 8, h["y"] + 18, esc(h["name"]), ) def edge_svg(e): """An edge as its ENDPOINTS, not as a finished path. There is deliberately no `d` attribute here. The orthogonal routing lives in the client (`client/surface.js`) because it is presentation, and a `d` computed on both sides would be one algorithm in two languages. The client reads these attributes and draws. """ return ( '' ) % ( esc(e["id"]), esc(e["from"]), esc(e["to"]), e.get("lane", 0), esc(e.get("condition") or ""), ) def frame(nodes, hives): """The `viewBox`: the whole drawing, plus a margin. Without it the SVG shows the top-left corner of a canvas that is thousands of pixels tall, and since the element is exactly the size of its container there is nothing to scroll. Reported as "not usable", and rightly: a picture you cannot see the bottom of is not a picture. With a viewBox the browser scales the whole arrangement into the frame on its own, before any JavaScript runs — so the canvas is legible even if the client never loads. Zoom and pan then ride on TOP of this as the camera transform, which is why the frame is derived from the content and never from the camera. """ xs = [n["x"] for n in nodes] + [h["x"] for h in hives] ys = [n["y"] for n in nodes] + [h["y"] for h in hives] if not xs: return (0, 0, NODE_W, NODE_H) right = max([n["x"] + NODE_W for n in nodes] + [h["x"] + h["w"] for h in hives]) bottom = max([n["y"] + NODE_H for n in nodes] + [h["y"] + h["h"] for h in hives]) x0 = min(xs) - PAD_SIDE y0 = min(ys) - PAD_TOP return (x0, y0, right - x0 + PAD_SIDE, bottom - y0 + PAD_BOT) def render(nodes, hives, edges, camera, title): box = frame(nodes, hives) parts = [ # `id` + `phx-hook` are the contract with `client/surface.js`, and they are # load-bearing rather than cosmetic: a LiveView hook mounts only on an # element that carries BOTH. Without them the client never runs — no edge # gets its `d` (the server deliberately sends endpoints, not paths) and # nothing can be dragged. That was the state of every join until # 2026-08-17, with all the server-side tests green, because they all # asserted about the markup and none about the seam. '
' % esc(title), '") parts.append( '
%d cells, %d hives, %d edges
' % (len(nodes), len(hives), len(edges)) ) parts.append("
") return "".join(parts) # --- the two passes ----------------------------------------------------------- def main(): doc = json.load(sys.stdin) body = doc.get("body") or {} env = doc.get("envelope") or {} header = env.get("header") or {} hop = header.get("hop") or {} ctx = header.get("context") or {} # WHICH PASS THIS IS, decided by edge authority and nothing else. # # `canvy_origin` is stamped by the hive's `./render -> ./store` edge, so it is # on the store's reply and on nothing an HTTP request carries. Deciding this by # inspecting the body instead — "did it parse as rows?" — turned every store # error into an infinite render/store loop that stopped only at the TTL. A # discriminator has to be unambiguous, and only an edge can make it so. if str(ctx.get("canvy_origin") or "") != "render": # ---- pass 1: a request came in. Ask the store for everything. req = body.get("surface") or {} # `columns` is REQUIRED by the store — a select without it answers # "missing columns array", which is how the loop above was found. out = store_op( "select", table="canvas", columns=["kind", "id", "x", "y", "z", "doc"], limit=100000, ) # The request rides along in `hop`, and the hive's `./render -> ./store` # edge promotes it into `context`. That promotion is not decoration: `hop` # survives exactly ONE edge, and pass 2 is two edges away # (render -> store -> render). Carrying it in `hop` alone looked right and # silently lost every drop — the box came back at its automatic position. out["header"]["event"] = str(req.get("event") or "") value = req.get("value") or {} out["header"]["moved_id"] = str(value.get("id") or "") out["header"]["moved_x"] = str(value.get("x") or "") out["header"]["moved_y"] = str(value.get("y") or "") out["header"]["cam"] = json.dumps(value.get("camera") or {}) return [out] # ---- pass 2: the store answered. rows = rows_of(body) if hop.get("error_code"): # A refused write. One corrective render, because a picture claiming a # position the database does not hold is worse than a visible failure. return [ surface_reply( {"error": "the canvas store refused a write: %s" % hop.get("error_code")} ) ] if rows is None: # The store answered, and it was not a result set. One visible failure, # never a retry: a retry against a store that just refused is a loop. return [ surface_reply( {"error": "the canvas store did not return rows: %s" % last_text(body)[:200]} ) ] saved = {} camera = (0, 0, 1000) graph = {} for r in rows: kind = r.get("kind") if kind == "node": try: saved[str(r.get("id"))] = (int(r.get("x") or 0), int(r.get("y") or 0)) except (TypeError, ValueError): continue elif kind == "camera": try: camera = ( int(r.get("x") or 0), int(r.get("y") or 0), int(r.get("z") or 1000), ) except (TypeError, ValueError): pass elif kind == "graph": graph = as_doc(r.get("doc")) raw_nodes = graph.get("nodes") or [] raw_edges = graph.get("edges") or [] if not isinstance(raw_nodes, list) or not isinstance(raw_edges, list): return [surface_reply({"error": "the topology snapshot is malformed"})] if not raw_nodes: return [ surface_reply( { "error": "no topology snapshot yet — the refresh timer has not " "run, or /colony/graph answered nothing" } ) ] edges = edge_lanes( [ { "id": str(e.get("id") or ""), "from": str(e.get("from") or "").strip("/"), "to": str(e.get("to") or "").strip("/"), "condition": e.get("condition"), } for e in raw_edges if isinstance(e, dict) ] ) # A move overrides both the saved position and the automatic one. This is # what keeps the picture and the database from disagreeing: the box is # rendered where it is written, from ONE input. # From `context`, not from `hop`: see the promotion in the hive's edge. moved_id = str(ctx.get("canvy_moved_id") or "") writes = [] if moved_id: try: mx, my = int(ctx.get("canvy_moved_x")), int(ctx.get("canvy_moved_y")) except (TypeError, ValueError): mx = my = None if mx is not None: saved[moved_id] = (mx, my) # Delete then insert, in one emission and in that order: a position is # presentation state, so the row is REPLACED rather than appended. The # no-delete promise protects what was said and what was learned; where # a rectangle sits is neither. writes.append( store_op("delete", table="canvas", where={"kind": "node", "id": moved_id}) ) writes.append( store_op( "insert", table="canvas", row={"kind": "node", "id": moved_id, "x": mx, "y": my}, ) ) nodes = [] for n in raw_nodes: if not isinstance(n, dict): continue path = str(n.get("path") or "").strip("/") if not path: continue ctype = str(n.get("cell_type") or "") fill, stroke = TYPE_COLOR.get(ctype, DEFAULT_COLOR) nodes.append( { "id": path, "name": path.rsplit("/", 1)[-1], "type": ctype, "fill": fill, "stroke": stroke, } ) pos = auto_layout(nodes, edges, saved) for n in nodes: n["x"], n["y"] = pos[n["id"]] hives = hive_boxes(nodes, pos) html = render(nodes, hives, edges, camera, graph.get("scope") or "/") return writes + [surface_reply({"html": html})] if __name__ == "__main__": out = main() sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(out if len(out) > 1 else out[0]))

description.purpose: THE surface. Turns whatever the canvas store holds into every tag the browser sees, and writes back the one position a drop moved.
description.use_when: Inside a canvy hive. This is the cell the URL names: /surface/<this cell's path>.
description.not_in_scope: It reads no database -- the layout and the topology snapshot arrive as a store reply, by message. It computes no edge PATH: the orthogonal routing lives in client/surface.js because it is presentation, and one algorithm in two languages is the duplication that avoids. It knows nothing about HTTP, sockets or LiveView.
examples: pass 1: a request -> one select over the canvas table
pass 2: the store's rows -> the whole SVG, plus the layout write when a drop moved something
